# Gray Swan AI

- Org: Gray Swan AI (legal name on site footer: Gray Swan Security Inc.)
- Website: https://www.grayswan.ai (Arena app: https://app.grayswan.ai/arena)
- Fetched: 2026-10-19
- Type: commercial AI red-teaming / security vendor, spun out of Carnegie Mellon (Matt Fredrikson CEO, Zico Kolter chief scientist/co-founder, Andy Zou), with Center for AI Safety co-founders on the team (launch press release, 2024-07-16).

## What they evaluate
- Jailbreak robustness of chat models (harmful-output elicitation; the original Sept-Oct 2024 "Jailbreaking Championship": 631 participants, 10,000 jailbreak submissions, 100,000 attempts, 25 models, $40,000 prizes; blog 2024-10-28).
- Agentic prompt-injection robustness: the Agent Red Teaming (ART) benchmark (four exploitation categories: confidentiality breaches, conflicting objectives, prohibited content, prohibited actions) and, from 2026, the Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) benchmark covering tool-calling, coding and computer/browser-use agents, with a "concealment" (stealth) criterion.
- Adaptive automated red-teaming of lab safeguards and models with the Shade attacker agent (jailbreaks, indirect prompt injection in coding/computer-use environments, and in Google's case CBRN-bio and cyber-misuse safeguard bypass).
- Products (site, fetched 2026-10-19): Arena ("world's largest adversarial AI red teaming network", claims 15,000+ red teamers and >3 million attack attempts), Shade (enterprise adaptive attack platform using "LLM-based adversarial agents"), Cygnal (runtime input/output filter), Cygnet (2024: a Llama-3-8B-Instruct finetune with circuit breakers; today listed as "weight-level safety training" offering for open-weight builders), "Adversarial Evaluation" for model builders ("The benchmarks frontier labs run before they ship").

## Methodology
- Crowdsourced arena competitions: anonymised target models (code-named after stars, e.g. "Polaris" = claude-3.7-sonnet:thinking), target behaviours released in waves, automated LLM judging calibrated with the sponsor (UK AISI calibrated judging and handled all manual break appeals in the March 8-April 6 2025 challenge), cash prizes for first breaks / most unique breaks / over-refusal flags. Metric: ASR = total breaks / total chats per model (results snapshot, 2025-05-09).
- Benchmark construction from competition data (arXiv 2507.20526, Sec. 2.3): stricter LLM-judge filtering of submissions, sample up to 5 high-quality attacks per behaviour x model -> ART dataset of 4,700 attacks across 44 behaviours; evaluated on 19 frontier LLMs; results reported as behaviour-level ASR at k=1, k=10, k=100 queries; transfer heat-maps across source/target models; "universal attack" clustering.
- IPI benchmark (arXiv 2603.15714; Opus 5 system card Sec. 5.2.1): attacks must achieve both the harmful action and concealment from the user; deterministic tool-call judge plus LLM judge for stealth/task completion; up to 5 agent steps with a "WorldSim" LLM simulating tool responses; browser scenarios rendered as HTML screenshots. After deduplication, 1,130 high-transfer attacks were selected for the benchmark Anthropic reports (Opus 5 card) / 2,679 curated benchmark attacks are listed by source model in the paper's Table 5. Reported at k=1, 10, 15 attempts. Gray Swan states it will "endeavor to deliver quarterly updates through continued red teaming competitions" to counter saturation.
- Shade adaptive attacker (as described in Anthropic system cards): "adaptive systems that combine search, reinforcement learning, and human-in-the-loop insights"; attacker is optimised on a previous set of models then transferred; reported as ASR after 1 attempt and after 200 attempts per scenario (Opus 4.5/4.6/5 cards).
- Google reports Gray Swan Shade results per attempt ("Attempt Success Rate") and per task ("Behavior Success Rate"), which Google maps to its own QSR/OSR metrics (Gemini 3.7 Flash FSF report, footnote 9; Gemini 4 Argon safety report Sec. 3.3).

## Open-source tools / datasets
- circuit-breakers — https://github.com/GraySwanAI/circuit-breakers — code for "Improving Alignment and Robustness with Circuit Breakers" (arXiv 2406.04313, NeurIPS 2024; Gray Swan + CMU + CAIS). Representation-rerouting training that cuts harmful-request compliance by ~87% on average across attacks on HarmBench for Llama-3-8B/Mistral-7B while preserving MT-Bench (Cygnet: MT-Bench 8.21 vs 8.05 base).
- nanoGCG — https://github.com/GraySwanAI/nanoGCG — lightweight PyTorch implementation of the GCG adversarial-suffix attack (Zou et al. 2023).
- ipi_arena_os ("ipi-arena-bench") — https://github.com/GraySwanAI/ipi_arena_os (paper cites github.com/grayswansecurity/ipi_arena_os) — MIT-licensed environment with 41 behaviours (18 tool, 15 coding, 8 browser), judges and multi-step loop; attack strings mostly withheld; 95 Qwen-only attacks released at https://huggingface.co/datasets/sureheremarv/ipi_arena_attacks.
- AgentHarm — https://huggingface.co/datasets/ai-safety-institute/AgentHarm — 110 malicious agent tasks (440 with augmentations), 11 harm categories, 104 tools; Gray Swan + UK AISI, ICLR 2025 (arXiv 2410.09024).
- Also listed on GitHub org: crf-benchmark, a fork of ethz-spylab/agentdojo, an OpenClaw Cygnal plugin, a litellm fork (descriptions not fetched; UNVERIFIED purpose of crf-benchmark).
- Not open: the ART benchmark attack set (Anthropic Opus 4.6 card: "Since this benchmark is held-out, we do not have access to the test scenarios or model generations"), Shade, Cygnal.

Access pattern: labs supply pre-release endpoints to Arena competitions (2507.20526: "several pre-release models at the time of the challenge, from OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Anthropic, Amazon, xAI, Meta, Cohere, and Mistral"); Gray Swan runs ART/IPI/Shade against lab endpoints and labs report the numbers in their own cards. Model-specific attack data goes to the respective lab; full datasets to UK AISI and US CAISI (2603.15714 abstract). Seven of 22 models in the 2025 challenge stayed anonymous "upon lab request".

## Why they are trusted / credibility signals
- Named in lab system cards: Gray Swan's May 2026 Series A release claims citation "in 11 recent frontier model system cards" from Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta; this file verified OpenAI o1 and GPT-5, Anthropic Sonnet 4.5 / Opus 4.5 / Opus 4.6 / Opus 5 and Google Gemini 3.7 Flash / Gemini 4 Argon directly.
- Government co-sponsorship and co-authorship: UK AISI (funding, judge calibration, appeals), US AISI/CAISI (co-judge; CAISI research blog 2026-03-23), NeurIPS-track paper (per the research page) with AISI co-authors.
- Public, dated leaderboards with raw counts (breaks/chats per model) and per-user prize tables; model-level ASR published for 22 models (7 anonymised at lab request).
- Peer-reviewed research lineage: GCG (2023), Representation Engineering, HarmBench, WMDP, Cybench, AgentHarm (ICLR 2025), Circuit Breakers (NeurIPS 2024), D-REX, "AI agents vs penetration testers" (Dec 2025, with Stanford).
- Funding/independence: $5.5M seed (Forbes, Nov 2024); $40M Series A co-led by Wing VC and Madrona (May 28 2026) with Snowflake Ventures, Samsung Next, HRT, Obvious. Note conflicts: Zico Kolter sits on OpenAI's board and chairs its Safety and Security Committee and "recuses himself from dealings between the two companies" (Forbes AU); labs are paying customers and co-sponsors, and ART/IPI attack sets are shared only with sponsoring labs and AISIs. The CASRAI guide (secondary) frames arena results as lab-scoped and lab-published rather than an independent audit.
- Compliance badges on site: SOC 2, Cyber Essentials.

## Notable findings (numbers)
- 2025 UK AISI Agent Red-Teaming Challenge (Mar 8-Apr 6 2025): ~1.8M attempts, ~2,000 participants, 62,000+ successful breaks, 22 LLMs, 44 behaviours in 4 waves, $171,800 prizes to 161 red-teamers; "100% behavior ASR" (every model broken on every behaviour). Overall ASR: claude-3.7-sonnet:thinking 1.47% (1,613/110,089), claude-3.7-sonnet 1.61%, claude-3.5-sonnet 1.85%, gpt-4o 2.41%, claude-3.5-haiku 2.44%, o3 2.50%, o1 2.56%, gpt-4.5-preview 2.58%, ..., grok-2 4.15%, o3-mini 4.23%, o3-mini-high 4.75%, llama-3.1-405b 5.89%, pixtral-large 6.23%, llama-3.3-70b 6.49%.
- ART paper Table 1 (ASR by category, direct / indirect / all): confidentiality 7.8 / 29.8 / 17.1; conflicting objectives 7.0 / - / 7.0; prohibited content 4.8 / 15.9 / 8.9; prohibited action 4.2 / 36.8 / 15.9; all 5.7 / 27.1 / 12.7. On the curated ART subset, single-query behaviour ASR is 20-60% per model and approaches ~100% by k=10 for most; attacks transfer to unseen models (Gemini 2.5 Pro, o4-mini); "limited correlation between agent robustness and model size, capability, or inference-time compute".
- IPI competition (2603.15714): 464 participants, ~272,000 attempts, 13 models, 41 scenarios, 8,648 successful attacks; ASR from 0.5% (Claude Opus 4.5) to 8.5% (Gemini 2.5 Pro); universal strategies transfer across 21/41 behaviours; attacks found against more robust models transfer to less robust ones but not vice versa (CAISI blog).
- "The Attacker Moves Second" (arXiv 2510.09023; OpenAI/Anthropic/GDM/ETH authors, not Gray Swan): adaptive RL/search attacks bypass 12 defenses, most with >90% ASR; 100% ASR against Circuit Breakers on HarmBench; MetaSecAlign 2% static -> 96% adaptive. Anthropic cites this paper as the reason to use Shade-style adaptive evaluations instead of static benchmarks.
- Circuit Breakers (2406.04313): ~87% average reduction in harmful-request compliance under attack for Llama-3-8B / Mistral-7B; Cygnet (Llama-3-8B finetune) roughly two orders of magnitude less harmful output; at the Oct 2024 championship Cygnet "largely withstood all jailbreaking attempts" but was broken by two participants (Forbes AU).
- o1 Jailbreak Arena (Dec 2024 card): 6% / 5% / 5% successful jailbreaks for harmful text / image-text / malicious code vs GPT-4o ~3.5% / 4% / 6%.
- GPT-5 bio jailbreak campaign: 0.98% ASR over 28,367 attempts; 96.7% of distinct jailbreaks caught by the generation monitor.

- app.grayswan.ai (Arena about page, live Agent Red-Teaming leaderboard) is behind a Vercel security checkpoint and returned 429/403 to WebFetch and curl; live leaderboard values were not captured (search snippet shows the same May 2025 ordering: Claude 3.7 Sonnet thinking 1.45%, Llama 3.3 70B 6.48% - UNVERIFIED).
- OpenAI o1 external-testers web page returned 403, but the o1 system card PDF (2024-12-05) was fetched and confirms the Jailbreak Arena section and the acknowledgement.
- No UK AISI (aisi.gov.uk) blog on the competition was found by search.
- Gray Swan claims citation in 11 system cards and lists ~25 model cards (incl. Meta Muse Spark, Reflection Beam, GPT-6 Astra, Claude 5.5 family); only the cards listed in the table above were fetched and checked.
- "Machine-in-the-Middle" cyber challenge (Nov 1-Dec 14 2025, $100k, sponsors Hack The Box/UK AISI/OpenAI/Anthropic/Amazon) and "Proving Ground" weekly challenges: known only from search snippets / nav text - UNVERIFIED details.
- The task premise that Gray Swan appears in the o3/o4-mini and ChatGPT agent system cards is NOT supported by the fetched PDFs (zero mentions); it is supported for GPT-5.
- Shade's internal methodology is only described second-hand in Anthropic/Google cards; no Gray Swan technical paper on Shade was found.
